title: T2 Filing Requirement Checker | Is a Return Owed at All
content:
The Requirement

T2 Filing Requirement Checker

A corporation files a T2 every year until it is formally dissolved. Three answers show whether a return is owed for this year.

Three answersCovers a dissolution yearNo activity is not an exemptionSays when nothing is owed

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

This tax year

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Rule Has No Activity Test In It

A corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. There is no threshold in that sentence and no exemption for a quiet year.

Which is why the question people ask, whether they have to file, nearly always has the same answer. The useful question is the one underneath it: what the return says when there is nothing to report. That is what a nil return is, and it is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

What People Think Exempts Them

Three beliefs account for most unfiled years, and none of them is right. No income, no bank account and never having started trading are all descriptions of a nil year rather than reasons there is no year.

The fourth is subtler and more costly: that a corporation nobody has touched for years has somehow lapsed. It has not. An unfiled year stays open, and the unfiled years checker lists the ones outstanding.

What people believeWhat it actually means
The corporation had no incomeA description of a nil year. The return is still owed
It has no bank accountThere is no asset test in the filing requirement
It never started tradingReturns are owed from incorporation, not from first sale
Nobody has touched it for yearsEvery one of those years is an unfiled year
It was dissolved mid-yearA final return is owed for the period up to that date
The year is before incorporationCorrect. There is no tax year and nothing to file

The One Case Where Nothing Is Owed

A year before incorporation is not an unfiled year. A tax year belongs to a corporation, so where there was no corporation there is no year and nothing to file.

That sounds obvious written down and it is worth stating, because a visitor counting backwards through years of silence often counts past the incorporation date. The years to file start there, not at the point the business stopped being active.

A Dissolution Year Is Still a Year

Where a corporation is dissolved part-way through a year, the period runs to the dissolution date and a return is owed for it. That return is the final T2 and it closes the record rather than being waived because the corporation has gone.

Dissolving with years outstanding leaves those years open behind it. The final T2 return due date calculator dates that last return, and the dissolution readiness checker tests whether the corporation is ready for the step.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a corporation with no activity have to file a T2?

Yes. A corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. Having nothing to report changes what the return says, not whether it is owed.

Does having no bank account exempt a corporation?

No. There is no activity test and no asset test in the filing requirement. A corporation with no bank account files a nil return.

What if the corporation never started trading?

It still files. A corporation that was incorporated and then left alone owes a return for every year since incorporation.

Do I owe a return for years before incorporation?

No. A tax year belongs to a corporation, so a year before the corporation existed is not an unfiled year.

Is a return owed for the year a corporation is dissolved?

Yes. The period runs to the dissolution date and the return for it is the final T2.

title: Required Schedules Checker | Which Schedules a Nil T2 Carries
content:
Schedules

Required Schedules Checker

Seven answers give the whole schedule set a nil return carries: the GIFI schedules, Schedule 24, Schedule 50, Schedule 8.

Seven answers, the whole setThe five GIFI triggersSchedule 50 at 10 percentAll of it inside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

What is on the books

Answer all seven questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Whole Set Behind One Set of Answers

Other tools here each test one schedule. This one asks what is on the books and returns the whole set, which is the order the question actually arrives in: nobody wonders about Schedule 50 in isolation.

Where you want one schedule in depth, the GIFI schedule requirement checker, the Schedule 50 shareholder threshold checker and the Schedule 8 CCA requirement checker each go further than this page does.

Five Things Withdraw the GIFI Permission

A corporation inactive all year with nothing to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes them required.

Five items, and one of them is enough. The permission is narrower than it first reads, because a corporation that was incorporated has share capital and a corporation with a bank account has held cash, which between them covers nearly every corporation that exists.

ScheduleWhat puts it on the returnInside the fee
GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141Any of share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank chargeYes
Schedule 24A first returnYes
Schedule 50Any shareholder at 10 percent or moreYes
Schedule 8 and loss continuityDepreciable property, or a loss carried forwardYes

The Three GIFI Schedules Travel Together

Schedules 100, 125 and 141 are the balance sheet, the income statement and the notes checklist. The permission to omit covers all three or none of them, so there is no position in which one goes on the return and the others stay off.

That is why a single bank charge matters out of proportion to its size. It is an item to report, so all three schedules are required, and two of them then carry mostly zeros.

Every Schedule Here Is Inside the Fee

The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the return the corporation actually needs: the T2 Short where it qualifies, GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 where they are required, Schedule 24 on a first return, Schedule 50 for every shareholder at 10 percent or more, Schedule 8 and loss continuity.

So the answer this page gives has no price attached to it. A return with every schedule required costs what a return with none of them costs, which is worth knowing before you worry about the count.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which schedules does a nil T2 return need?

It depends on what is on the books. GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 where any of five items is present, Schedule 24 on a first return, Schedule 50 for any shareholder at 10 percent or more, and Schedule 8 with loss continuity where there is depreciable property or a carried loss.

Can a nil return omit the GIFI schedules?

Only where none of five items is on the books. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required; the permission to omit them belongs to a corporation inactive all year with nothing to report.

When is Schedule 50 required?

Schedule 50 is tied to any shareholder at 10 percent or more, and it names every shareholder who meets that test.

When does Schedule 24 go on a return?

On a first return, and only on that one. A corporation filing for the first time carries it whether or not the first year had any activity.

Do more schedules cost more?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the schedules the return requires, however many that turns out to be.

title: Share Capital Reporting Checker | GIFI and Schedule 50
content:
Share Capital

Share Capital Reporting Checker

Share capital makes the GIFI schedules required even with no activity. Three answers show what the shares on your books trigger.

Issued at incorporationMakes GIFI requiredSchedule 50 at 10 percentDoes not stop a year being nil

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The shares

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Share Capital Is the First of the Five Triggers

A corporation inactive all year with nothing to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141. Share capital is the first of the five things that withdraw that permission, alongside cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost and a bank charge.

It is also the one that catches the most corporations, for a reason that has nothing to do with trading: shares are issued at incorporation. A corporation that has never done anything since still has share capital on its books.

The five triggersHow a dormant corporation usually acquires it
Share capitalShares issued at incorporation
CashA bank account opened and never closed
A shareholder loanMoney put in to cover a cost, never repaid
An incorporation costThe cost of setting the corporation up
A bank chargeA monthly fee on the account nobody uses

Share Capital Does Not Stop a Year Being Nil

These are two different questions and they get run together. Share capital sits on the balance sheet. Whether a year is nil is a question about the income statement, and shares issued years ago say nothing about whether this year had income.

A dormant corporation with shares issued and no activity is the ordinary nil case, not an exception to it. What it means is that the return carries the GIFI schedules with the share capital on them, and the figures for the year are zero.

Schedule 50 Runs Off a Threshold, Not Off Control

Schedule 50 is tied to any shareholder at 10 percent or more. It is not a schedule about the controlling shareholder, and it does not list the largest one: it names every shareholder who meets the test.

A corporation with one shareholder holding everything files it for that person. A corporation with twelve shareholders at 8 percent each files none. The Schedule 50 shareholder threshold checker works through the threshold properly.

A Dividend Takes the Year Out of Nil

Paying or receiving a dividend is activity. A corporation that did either is not filing a nil return for that year, whatever else was quiet about it.

That is a boundary of this service rather than a complication within it. Such a year goes to Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year, and the nil return versus full return checker is where that line is drawn in full.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does share capital make the GIFI schedules required?

Yes. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required, even where the corporation had no activity.

My corporation has never traded. Does it have share capital?

Almost certainly. Shares are normally issued at incorporation, so a corporation that has done nothing since still has share capital on its books. Check the incorporation documents rather than memory.

Does share capital mean the year is not nil?

No. Share capital is a balance sheet item. Whether a year is nil turns on the income statement, so a dormant corporation with shares issued files an ordinary nil return.

Who goes on Schedule 50?

Every shareholder at 10 percent or more, not only the largest or the one with control.

What if a dividend was paid?

Then the year is not nil. A corporation that paid or received a dividend is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

title: Shareholder Loan Balance Checker | What It Means for a Nil Return
content:
Shareholder Loan

Shareholder Loan Balance Checker

A shareholder loan balance makes the GIFI schedules required even with no activity. Three answers show what yours triggers.

Either direction countsA still balance countsDoes not stop a year being nilReporting, not tax treatment

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The balance

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Balance Sitting Still Is Still Something

A corporation inactive all year with nothing to report may omit GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141. A shareholder loan is one of the five things that make them required, and nothing in that turns on whether the balance moved.

So a loan that has sat unchanged for six years is reportable in the seventh. The corporation has something to report, which is the test, and a dormant year does not empty the balance sheet.

Either Direction Is a Shareholder Loan Here

Money the corporation owes its shareholder and money the shareholder owes the corporation are both a shareholder loan balance for this purpose. Bookkeeping distinguishes them and the reporting trigger does not.

Which settles the question people arrive with. Whether the balance is a due-to or a due-from, the answer about the GIFI schedules is the same.

The balanceWhat it is calledMakes GIFI required
The corporation owes the shareholderA due-to-shareholder balanceYes
The shareholder owes the corporationA due-from-shareholder balanceYes
A balance that did not move all yearStill a shareholder loan balanceYes
No balance either wayNothing to report on this groundNo

A Loan Does Not Stop a Year Being Nil

A loan balance is a balance sheet item, not income. A dormant corporation carrying one files an ordinary nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, with the GIFI schedules on it.

The thing to separate is the balance from the movement. A balance is reported. Money moving in a year is activity, and activity is where the question of whether the year is nil starts to need a real answer.

What This Page Deliberately Does Not Say

It answers a reporting question: whether the schedules go on the return. It says nothing about how a shareholder loan is taxed, what happens if it is outstanding too long, or what interest it should carry.

Those turn on facts a web page does not have, and getting them wrong is expensive. Where a loan raises them it belongs with Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca rather than with a nil filing, which is a return rather than advice.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a shareholder loan make the GIFI schedules required?

Yes. A shareholder loan is one of the five things that make GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required, even where the corporation had no activity.

What if the balance did not change all year?

It still counts. The permission to omit the schedules belongs to a corporation inactive all year with nothing to report, and a balance is something to report.

Does the direction of the loan matter?

Not for this. A balance the corporation owes its shareholder and one the shareholder owes the corporation are both a shareholder loan balance here.

Does a shareholder loan stop the year being nil?

No. It is a balance sheet item rather than income, so a dormant corporation carrying one files an ordinary nil return.

How is a shareholder loan taxed?

That is outside what this page answers and outside a nil filing. It turns on facts a web page does not have, and it belongs with Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca.

title: GIFI Schedule 125 Checker | The Income Statement on a Nil Year
content:
Schedule 125

GIFI Schedule 125 Checker

Schedule 125 is the income statement. Three answers show whether it goes on a nil return and whether it carries a figure.

The income statementA bank charge is an expenseAll three or noneZeros are an answer

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The year’s figures

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Schedule 125 Is the Income Statement

Of the three GIFI schedules, 100 is the balance sheet, 125 is the income statement and 141 is the notes checklist. Schedule 125 is the one that reports what the year did rather than what the corporation holds.

Which is why people expect it to be the blank one on a dormant year. Often it very nearly is, and nearly blank is not the same as absent. The nil GIFI balance sheet checker covers the other side, Schedule 100.

GIFI scheduleWhat it carriesOn a dormant year
Schedule 100The balance sheetShare capital, cash and any loan balance
Schedule 125The income statementZeros, unless there was a bank charge or another expense
Schedule 141The notes checklistWho prepared the statements, and that they were neither audited nor reviewed

A Bank Charge Is an Expense

This is the fact worth carrying away. A corporation with no revenue, no staff and no customers still has an income statement with a figure on it if the bank took a monthly fee off the account.

It is a few dollars and it is an expense, so the year has something to report. A corporation with an open bank account usually has one of these, which is how a year that feels like nothing turns out to have a number in it.

The Permission Covers All Three or None

The permission runs to the three schedules together, which is the part that decides this page. There is no position where Schedule 100 goes on the return and Schedule 125 stays off, so an item on the balance sheet puts the income statement on the return too, carrying zeros.

What withdraws the permission is any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge. What holds it open is a corporation inactive all year with nothing to report, and share capital alone is enough to take it away.

Zeros on a Required Schedule Are Not a Problem

A Schedule 125 of zeros is a complete schedule rather than an incomplete one. It reports that the year had no revenue and no expense, which is a fact about the year and the thing a nil return exists to say.

A nil return is not an empty return. It is a full return whose figures are zero, which is why it carries the schedules the corporation needs and why all of them are inside the fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is GIFI Schedule 125?

The income statement. Schedule 100 is the balance sheet, Schedule 125 is the income statement and Schedule 141 is the notes checklist.

Can a nil return leave Schedule 125 off?

Only where the corporation was inactive all year with nothing to report. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required.

Does a bank charge count?

Yes. A bank charge is an expense, so it puts a figure on the income statement and it is one of the five things that make the GIFI schedules required.

Can Schedule 100 be filed without Schedule 125?

No. The permission to omit covers all three GIFI schedules together, so they go on the return as a set.

Is a schedule of zeros acceptable?

Yes. A nil return is a full return whose figures are zero, and a Schedule 125 of zeros reports that the year had no revenue and no expense.

title: GIFI Schedule 141 Checker | The Notes Checklist on a Nil Return
content:
Schedule 141

GIFI Schedule 141 Checker

Schedule 141 records who prepared the statements and what work stands behind them. Three answers show what yours says.

The notes checklistWho prepared the statementsAudited, reviewed or neitherNeither is a complete answer

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The statements

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Schedule 141 Describes the Statements, Not the Figures

Schedules 100 and 125 carry the numbers. Schedule 141 is the notes checklist: it records who put the financial statements together and what level of work stands behind them.

So it is the one schedule in the set that is about the preparation rather than the corporation. The guide to GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 sets out what each of the three carries.

What Schedule 141 recordsThe usual answer on a dormant corporation
Who prepared the financial statementsThe firm that prepared the return
Whether they were auditedNo
Whether they were reviewedNo
Whether any assurance work was performedNone, which is a complete answer on a nil return

Neither Audited Nor Reviewed Is the Normal Answer

For a dormant corporation the honest answer to the assurance question is usually neither, and that is a complete answer rather than a gap in the return.

A nil return does not need an audit or a review behind it. Reading the schedule as though it were asking for one is what makes people think a quiet corporation needs an engagement it does not need.

It Is Required on the Same Trigger as the Other Two

Schedule 141 has no test of its own. It goes on the return whenever Schedules 100 and 125 do, and it comes off only when they do, so the question is never about this schedule in particular.

That shared trigger is any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge, against a permission that belongs to a corporation inactive all year with nothing to report. In practice the schedule is nearly always required, because a corporation with shares issued has share capital.

On a Return Filed Here, the Preparer Question Has One Answer

Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, a registered EFILE electronic filer. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

So the preparer side of the schedule is settled the same way on every return filed through this site, and preparing both the statements and the schedule describing them is inside the fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is GIFI Schedule 141?

The notes checklist. It records who prepared the financial statements and what level of work stands behind them, where Schedules 100 and 125 carry the figures.

Does a nil return need an audit or a review?

No. Neither audited nor reviewed is the normal answer for a dormant corporation and it is a complete answer.

When is Schedule 141 required?

On the same trigger as the other two GIFI schedules. Any share capital, cash, shareholder loan, incorporation cost or bank charge makes all three required.

Is there a separate test for Schedule 141?

No. It goes on the return whenever Schedules 100 and 125 do.

Who is recorded as preparing the statements?

On a return filed here, Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation, which prepares and transmits in Canada as a registered EFILE electronic filer.

The corporation as it stands

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Three Tools on This Subject, and Which One You Want

Dormancy comes up in three different questions and there is a tool for each. This one lists what is still owed while the corporation stays open.

The dormant corporation test decides whether the corporation is dormant in the first place. The CRA account closure sequencer gives the order for shutting the accounts down. The corporate deadline calendar generator puts dates on the obligations this page lists.

What you want to knowThe tool that answers it
Whether the corporation counts as dormantDormant corporation test
What is still owed while it stays openThis page
The order for closing the CRA accountsCRA account closure sequencer
The dates those obligations fall onCorporate deadline calendar generator

Nothing Lapses Because Nobody Is Looking

A corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. Being dormant is not a status that suspends that, and no amount of time passing turns it into one.

The registry annual return runs alongside it on its own date. Two obligations, two bodies, two consequences for missing them, and neither of them stops because the corporation has gone quiet.

An Open Account Keeps Generating Returns

A payroll account expects a T4 information return even where nobody was paid, and a GST/HST account expects returns including nil ones. The obligation follows the open account rather than the activity.

Form RC145 closes either of them. An inactive T2 does not close those accounts, which is the mistake worth avoiding: filing the tax return does not tell the payroll account to stop expecting something.

One of These Is Inside the Fee

The nil T2 is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The registry annual return, any T4 return and any GST/HST return sit outside it, as does closing an account.

Which is said here rather than in the small print because a visitor reading a list of obligations should be able to see, in the same table, which one this service takes off their hands.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does a dormant corporation still have to file?

A T2 every year until it is formally dissolved, the annual return to its registry, and returns on any payroll or GST/HST account that is still open.

Does being dormant suspend the filing requirement?

No. A corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved.

Does filing a nil T2 close my payroll account?

No. An inactive T2 does not close those accounts. Form RC145 closes a payroll or a GST/HST account.

Is the registry annual return part of the tax return?

No. It is a separate filing to a separate body, reporting the directors and the registered office rather than any income.

Which of these is covered by the fee?

The nil T2 return, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The registry annual return, T4 returns, GST/HST returns and account closures are outside it.

title: Annual Return vs Tax Return Checker | Two Different Filings
content:
Two Filings

Annual Return vs Tax Return Checker

The annual return and the T2 are unrelated filings to different bodies. Two answers set them side by side.

Side by sideDifferent bodies, different datesDifferent consequencesOnly one is in the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

Where the corporation is registered

Answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Filings at a Minimum, and One Shared Word

Every corporation owes at least two: a tax return, and an annual return to the registry that holds it. The annual return and the tax return share a word and nothing else. One confirms the directors and the registered office to the registry that holds the corporation. The other reports the year’s figures to the Canada Revenue Agency.

Nearly every confusion on this subject comes from the shared noun. Once they are set beside each other the overlap turns out to be the word, which is why this page is a comparison rather than an explanation.

The T2The annual return
What it isA corporate income tax returnA registry filing
Filed withThe Canada Revenue AgencyThe registry the corporation is incorporated with
What it reportsThe year’s figuresThe directors and the registered office
Missing itThe tax year stays openThe corporation can be struck from the register
Inside the feeYesNo

Filing One Does Nothing for the Other

A corporation can be up to date on its annual returns and have six years of unfiled T2 returns behind it. The registry is satisfied and the tax years are open, because the registry never told the Canada Revenue Agency anything.

It runs the other way too. Every T2 filed on time does not stop a corporation being struck from the register for missing the annual return, which the involuntary dissolution risk checker covers.

The Federal Annual Return Has a Date and a Fee

A federal corporation files its annual return within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary, and the fee is $12.00. It is a government fee and HST does not apply to it.

Note what that date runs from. The anniversary, not the fiscal year-end, so the two filings can sit months apart and both be on time. The federal annual return anniversary calculator works out the dates.

Only One of Them Is Inside the Fee

The nil T2 is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The annual return is a registry filing and is not covered by it, which is stated plainly here rather than discovered later.

That is not a gap in the service so much as a different counter. A registry filing is made to the registry, and a corporation can make it itself in a few minutes once it knows the date.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the annual return the same as the tax return?

No. The annual return is a registry filing confirming the directors and the registered office. The T2 is a corporate income tax return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency.

Does filing my T2 cover the annual return?

No. They go to different bodies and neither one satisfies the other.

When is the federal annual return due?

Within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary. That date runs from the anniversary rather than the fiscal year-end.

How much is the federal annual return?

$12.00. It is a government fee and HST does not apply to it.

What happens if I miss each one?

An unfiled T2 leaves the tax year open, invites a demand to file and blocks a clearance certificate. A missed annual return can get the corporation struck from the register.

title: Dissolve or Keep Filing Cost Calculator | Both Routes Priced
content:
The Decision

Dissolve or Keep Filing Cost Calculator

Keeping a dormant corporation costs a return every year. Enter the years to compare that with winding it up.

Both routes side by sideTotals the years of filingNames what is outside the feeUnfiled years come first

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The decision

Enter the number of years and answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Keeping a Dormant Corporation Is a Recurring Cost

A corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. Holding an empty corporation is therefore a decision to pay for a return annually for as long as it exists.

Which is often the right decision. There are good reasons to hold a name, a history or a registration. It is worth seeing as a subscription rather than as a formality, and that is what the left column of the comparison does.

One Side Totals and the Other Does Not

The returns are priced here, so the cost of staying open totals exactly. Winding up involves a clearance certificate request and the registry articles of dissolution, and neither is covered by this fee.

So the comparison names those steps rather than putting a figure on them. A page that invented a total for the dissolution side would be more satisfying to read and less use to rely on.

StepWhich routePriced here
A nil T2 for each year it stays openKeep filingYes, $300.00 plus HST per tax year
The registry annual return each yearKeep filingNo, a government fee
The final T2 for the period ending at dissolutionWind upYes, $300.00 plus HST
A clearance certificate requestWind upNo
The registry articles of dissolutionWind upNo

Unfiled Years Come First on Either Route

Where years are already outstanding the choice narrows, because both routes start in the same place. A clearance request rests on a complete filing record, and dissolving a corporation that still owes returns leaves those tax years open behind it.

The catch-up filing schedule generator dates the outstanding years and the unfiled years cost calculator totals them. Those come before this decision rather than after it.

What Each Route Actually Ends

Filing for another five years ends nothing. At the end of it the corporation is still on the register and the same question arrives again, five years of fees later.

A completed wind-up ends the obligation. That is the difference the right-hand column is really reporting, and it is worth more weight than the arithmetic. The dissolution readiness checker tests whether the corporation is ready for it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it cheaper to dissolve a corporation or keep filing?

Keeping it costs $300.00 plus HST per tax year for as long as it exists, plus the registry annual return. Winding up is one final return plus a clearance request and the registry dissolution, and those two are not covered by this fee.

Why does the comparison not total both sides?

Because only one side is priced here. The returns are; a clearance request and the registry articles of dissolution are not, so the page names them rather than inventing a figure.

Can I dissolve without filing the outstanding years?

Dissolving a corporation that still owes returns leaves those tax years open behind it, and a clearance request rests on a complete filing record. Both routes start with the outstanding years.

What does a nil return cost each year?

$300.00 plus HST per tax year, for one corporation for one tax year.

Is there a reason to keep a dormant corporation?

Often, yes. Holding a name, a history or a registration can be worth the annual cost. The point of the comparison is to show what that cost is.

Annual Return

Federal Annual Return Fee Calculator

The federal annual return is $12.00 within 60 days of the anniversary. Enter the incorporation date for a dated schedule.

$12.00 a yearNo HST on a government feeRuns from the anniversaryOutside the nil T2 fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 30, 2026

The corporation

Enter the incorporation date and how many years to list.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Numbers, and Neither Moves

A federal corporation files its annual return within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary, and the fee is $12.00. Both are fixed, which makes this the most predictable obligation a corporation has.

It is a government fee and HST does not apply to it. So the total this page gives is the total: there is no tax line to add to it, unlike every other price on the site.

ItemThe federal annual return
Fee$12.00
HST on the feeNone. It is a government fee
DueWithin 60 days of the incorporation anniversary
Measured fromThe incorporation anniversary, not the year-end
Filed withCorporations Canada
Inside the nil T2 feeNo

The Date Runs From the Anniversary

Not from the fiscal year-end, which is what makes this obligation drift out of sight. A corporation whose T2 is due in December and whose anniversary falls in March has two filing dates nine months apart, every year, both correct.

Changing the fiscal year-end does not move this date either. The federal annual return anniversary calculator works out a single year’s dates in more detail than the table here does.

It Is Not a Tax Return and Missing It Is a Different Problem

The annual return reports the directors and the registered office to Corporations Canada. It reports no income and no tax, and filing it says nothing to the Canada Revenue Agency.

Missing it does not create an unfiled tax year. It puts the corporation at risk of being struck from the register, which is a different consequence with a different cure. The annual return versus tax return checker sets the two filings side by side.

Outside the Nil T2 Fee, and Small

This filing is not covered by the nil T2 fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year. It is a registry filing, made to the registry, and a corporation can make it itself once it knows the date.

Which is the practical reason this page exists. At $12.00 the fee is not the problem. Not knowing the date is, and a corporation struck off for the want of a $12.00 filing has an expensive problem from a cheap cause.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is the federal annual return?

$12.00. It is a government fee and HST does not apply to it.

When is it due?

Within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary.

Does the date move if I change my fiscal year-end?

No. It runs from the incorporation anniversary, so it does not follow the fiscal year-end.

Is the annual return covered by the nil T2 fee?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the nil T2 return. The annual return is a separate registry filing.

What happens if I miss it?

It does not create an unfiled tax year. It puts the corporation at risk of being struck from the register.
